_pullQuote: BORROWED, and labelled as borrowed (Cole, 2026-08-19). The Black has zero reviews of its own: no rating in products.json, no pull in _src/data/reviews/. This is verbatim from the lgw01-gold Judge.me pull, and the `who` line names the Gold so nobody reads it as proof of a product that has none. TITLE AND QUOTE ARE THE SAME REVIEW — Ray O.'s own title, Ray O.'s own words. Chosen over the stronger feel-and-spin reviews because they are titled after the gold finish or untitled, and a quote praising the shine on the page that argues for no shine fights the page. Five stars, which the curated-moment floor requires and the card's markup hard-codes.

buyBody: The Carver comes off the face soft, grabs the ball hard enough to stop it near where you aimed, and tells you honestly when you didn't. The Black does all of it with gold left only on the clover and the loft stamp, which is the whole difference. Six lofts, right hand, sixty days to decide whether it stays in the bag.

clubHeadline: All the spin, none of the shine. Rip it back and say nothing.
clubParas: The Black is the same wedge as the Gold in a finish that keeps to itself. Forged 1020 soft carbon steel gives it the buttery feel and the honest feedback, and the dual-texture face grips the ball everywhere rather than only in the grooves, so the check-up shows up out of wet grass and on the strikes you didn't catch pure. Blacked out heel to toe with gold left on the clover and the loft stamp, it sits down into the grass at address and stays there.

clubSpecs.v: High spin in any conditions, soft feel, and a head that gives away nothing at address.
Forged 1020 head with a dual-texture face: CNC-milled grooves, micro-milled between, sandblasted across. Blacked out, with gold on the clover, the wordmark and the loft stamp.
Right hand today. Left hand is coming.
Any golfer who would rather the club said nothing. Same short game as the Gold, none of the conversation on the next tee.

videoBrief: 16:9 product film, 40–60s. The pitch is the finish, so shoot it at address in changing light. The club should read almost invisible against grass and then catch the gold on the stamp as it moves.

look.headline: The one nobody notices until you use it
paras: Gold clubs get comments. That is fine until it is not, and there is a kind of golfer who would rather the club said nothing at all.
This is that club. It still has gold on it, on the clover and the number, but you have to be standing over it to find any.
If that isn't you, the Carver 01 Gold catches every bit of light there is.
look.aside: Everyone else is carrying the same club with someone else's name on it. It's better to be lucky.

helpLoft.sub: Wedges work in gaps. Four to six degrees between clubs keeps your distances even and stops two wedges going the same yardage. Tell us the loft of your pitching wedge and we'll do the arithmetic.

_01: THE 01, BLACK. Same club as the gold on the LGW01 platform (v1.8's platform note), K grind, six lofts. $109 rather than $99 because the blacked-out finish is a real extra process — the one price difference in the wedge line that stands for something (Cole 2026-07-31).

GRIND COPY — sourced, no longer a draft.
1. SOURCE IS THE SPEC-TO-BENEFIT TRANSLATION GUIDE v1.0 (Cole supplied it 2026-08-01, references-spec-to-benefit-v1.0.md). It defines both grinds directly: K is "a wider, flatter sole profile with a standard leading edge... the no-surprises wedge... built for the golfer who strikes cleanly and plays primarily from standard lies"; S is "a narrower, more relieved sole with a reshaped leading edge... the versatility wedge... tight lies, awkward angles, open-face lobs".
2. THIS REVERSES AN EARLIER CORRECTION. HANDOFF §24d recorded that the S is NOT the open-face versatility grind, on the basis that our letters are Vokey's and that is Vokey's M. Lucky's own written guide says otherwise, and a company document about what Lucky's specs mean outranks an inference from another maker's nomenclature. The site now follows the guide. If Cole wants the Vokey reading back, this is the block to change.
3. IT ALSO CLOSES §24a's open question. "Is our S actually narrower, does it have a tapered rear sole" is answered in writing: narrower, more relieved, reshaped leading edge. This block is no longer the unverified one.
4. Every number in `facts` is still the manufacturer sheet, and the measured-vs-effective bounce note still stands — a narrow relieved sole carrying more measured bounce than a wide flat one is exactly what the geometry predicts.
_club: Takomo-shaped 2026-08-19, matching the Gold (HANDOFF 36c): playful two-beat headline, ONE intro paragraph, the grind as a labelled sub-block, then Takomo's bullets ending on For who and HCP range. The standalone `grinds` section is deleted from this page: pdp.js already sends the buy box's 'Which grind?' link to #club. Three stale claims went with the old copy: the club called itself 'the LGW02' (the site calls it the Carver 01 Black everywhere else), it said the gold 'stops at three' lofts (the merged 01 Gold has six), and the close typed the price into editorial.

clubGrinds.v: A wider, flatter sole with a standard leading edge. Set up square, take your divot, get the same result every time. Built for standard lies: fairway, rough, fringe. It is the only grind the Black is built in, at all six lofts. The S, narrower and relieved so the face can open on tight lies and lobs, is on the Gold.

_specTabs: Takomo-shaped 2026-08-19 to match the Gold: three cards (Clubs / Shafts / Grips), each a caption, a stacked key/value head and a black-header matrix. Bounce in Takomo's suffix notation with our letter (8K), so the sheet speaks the picker's language. The old shape was Club / By loft / Shaft & grip and carried two things that had to go: a PRICE row (price is per variant, from products.json, and is never retyped in editorial) and a K-vs-S aside on a club that is only built in K. NOTHING the Product Reference Guide does not publish is on the page: no swing weight, tip diameter or grip length.
_grinds: The standalone grind section was deleted 2026-08-19, the same move the Gold made: with the grind now a labelled sub-block inside the description, a whole section for ONE grind was a page of scroll saying what four lines say. Its one genuinely useful sentence, that the S lives on the Gold, moved into the K sub-block. pdp.js already points 'Which grind?' at #club.
